channel.title: Honest Guide (English)
channel.description: HTTP headers, cookies and browser dev tools, explained

item.title: HSTS rollout order: ramp up max-age in three stages before you preload
item.description: A safe order for rolling out Strict-Transport-Security: check every subdomain, ramp max-age from 5 minutes to 1 month, then decide on preload, which hstspreload.org says cannot easily be undone.

item.title: Content-Security-Policy Report-Only: the safe way to send your first CSP
item.description: How to send a CSP as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only so violations are reported without blocking anything, why report-to is required, and what to fix before you switch to enforcing.

item.title: CORS errors in local development: the response headers that matter
item.description: A short map of the CORS response headers your server must send for simple requests, preflights and credentialed requests, with the browser error message each missing header produces.

item.title: Copy a web page table into a spreadsheet with XPath and the Console, no scraper needed
item.description: A short DevTools snippet that turns table rows into tab-separated text you can paste into a spreadsheet, how relative XPath per column works, and when you should not collect data from a page at all.

item.title: Test an XPath in Chrome DevTools: $x(), Elements search and document.evaluate
item.description: Three ways to try an XPath on a live page in Chrome, with copy-paste examples for text, attributes and the nth item, plus the one mistake that makes //li[1] return many nodes.

item.title: Header changes not working in Manifest V3? What changed and what still works
item.description: Chrome removed blocking webRequest for most extensions in Manifest V3. How header edits work now with declarativeNetRequest, and a short checklist for rules that do nothing.

item.title: Cookie editor export to cookies.txt: the 7 fields curl expects
item.description: If your cookie editor gave you a JSON list, curl still wants a tab-separated file with seven fields. How each Chrome cookie property maps to them, with a small script.

item.title: Moving header rules to a new tool: why "append" fails on some request headers in Chrome
item.description: Chrome only allows the append operation on 21 listed request headers. Which ones, what to use instead, and three other things to check after you move your rules.

item.title: ModHeader was removed from the Chrome Web Store: what was reported, and how to check any header extension
item.description: Google removed ModHeader on 10 July 2026 after Stripe OLT found a dormant browsing-history collector. What the report says, what it does not say, and a 2-minute permission check.

item.title: Chrome extension permissions: what "site access" means and how to limit it
item.description: How to read a Chrome extension's permissions before installing: host permissions, activeTab, optional permissions, and the three site-access settings you can change yourself.

item.title: How to view and edit cookies in Chrome (DevTools, or an extension)
item.description: Open DevTools, go to Application > Storage > Cookies, pick the site, and double-click a field to edit it. When an extension is the better choice, and what permissions it needs.

item.title: How to change HTTP headers in Chrome (response headers in DevTools, request headers with an extension)
item.description: DevTools can override response headers locally (Network > right-click > Override headers). To add or change request headers, you need an extension that uses declarativeNetRequest.

item.title: SameSite cookies explained: Strict, Lax and None (and why None needs Secure)
item.description: Strict sends a cookie only on same-site requests, Lax also on some top-level navigations, None on every request but only with Secure. What Chrome does when SameSite is missing.

item.title: Security headers checklist: the 7 to add and the 5 to remove
item.description: Check for HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and COOP, and remove X-Powered-By, server versions, X-XSS-Protection, HPKP and Expect-CT.
